resources.string: Either the off switch is on or the fix hasn\'t started yet. The correction log shows which.
Fix is ON (root mode, not installed)
Root mode starts by itself after a restart, once root is on.
The installer only works on the Sonim XP3800 with Android 8.1.\n\nThis phone: Android %1$s, XP3800 keypad %2$s.
Installs the fix permanently. Installing needs root; the fix then runs without root. Or install from a computer (see the README).
Removes the permanent install. It needs root; without root, Turn off / on can turn the fix off instead.
The fix is already installed. To reinstall, use Undo, restart the phone, then install again.

Check install reruns the install\'s final checks with root, changing nothing: the stock policy backup (.bak) is the stock policy with its stock label, and /system holds what was installed. Use it after an install that showed \"failed\" after \"Installed. Reboot to start it.\"

Before you start, have a backup of the system partition and an EDL flashing setup, in case the phone won't boot.

Installs the fix permanently, so the filter runs at every boot without root:
• Backs up the stock SELinux policy as .bak files in /system/etc/selinux. Undo restores from them.
• Checks that the new policy compiles, and stops without changing anything if it doesn't.
• Installs the filter and its policy rule.

Dry run only does the check, without changing anything.
The fix isn\'t installed, so there\'s nothing to undo.

Removes the permanent install: puts the stock SELinux policy back from the .bak backup and deletes the filter. Restart afterwards to finish.\n\nIf the phone won\'t boot afterwards, flash your system backup over EDL.
Turn the fix off or on

Turns the installed fix off or on without uninstalling it. When it's off, the keypad works as it did before.

From a computer:

Off:
adb shell touch /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot

On:
adb shell rm /data/local/tmp/keydebounce.off
adb reboot
Turns the installed fix off or on. The fix isn\'t installed; to stop root mode, use Run with root ▸ Stop.
With root, Off now and On now switch it right away, without a restart.

Runs the filter through root, without installing anything. Start turns it on until the next restart, and Stop turns it off.\n\nBoot sets Start at boot (now %1$s), which turns the filter on by itself after each restart. With Root Manager it waits until about 5 minutes after power-on, when the phone has calmed down, before starting root.
Runs the filter through root, without installing anything. The fix is installed, so it already runs at every boot.
Runs the filter through root, without installing anything. It needs root.

Drops the extra press when one key press registers twice (contact bounce), without root. It doesn't fix key overlap; the root filter does.

Turn it on in Accessibility ▸ %2$s. Or from a computer:

adb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1
adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services %1$s/.BounceFilterService

That command replaces the list of accessibility services that are on. If others are on (see: adb shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services), include them too, separated by a colon (:).

Turn it off in Accessibility ▸ %2$s.

On this phone, turning it on or off only takes effect after a restart.

No-root fallback that only fixes contact bounce (a key registering twice from one press). It does not fix key overlap (two keys pressed close together); that still needs the root daemon. See the README on GitHub.
Start at boot is %1$s.\n\nTurns the filter on by itself after each restart, with nothing to tap. With a root that\'s on at boot (Magisk), it starts right away.

With Root Manager, it waits until about 5 minutes after power-on, then starts root and the filter. If starting root ever crashes the phone, the next restarts ask first (Start / Not now) until a start works.

Starting root at boot crashed the phone before (Root Manager\'s exploit), so the app asks instead of trying by itself, on every restart until a start works.\n\nStart tries now. Not now leaves it off; the next restart asks again.
Boot notification is %1$s.\n\nShows a silent notification when Start at boot starts the filter, and then whether it came on. You can swipe it away.
Start at boot notification is on.
Start at boot notification is off.
Start at boot is starting root and the filter.
Start at boot is starting the filter.
Start at boot couldn\'t start it: %1$s
Start at boot is on. It takes effect after a restart.
Root hasn\'t started since the phone restarted. Start root starts it (Root Manager\'s exploit runs once and can crash and restart the phone), then runs this.
With the fix installed, it crashes more often.
Start at boot is on. After a restart the filter starts by itself once root is on.
Couldn\'t restart (%s). Restart with the power key.
Granted. Press Close: the app closes so the permission takes effect. Then open it again.

The correction log needs permission to read the phone's log. Grant with root gives the app that permission.

Without root, from a computer:
adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS
Not run: root hasn\'t started since the restart, and starting it runs Root Manager\'s kernel exploit, which can crash the phone. Nothing was changed.
No result: root wasn\'t available, was refused, or stopped partway. If there\'s no output above, nothing was changed; otherwise the output shows how far it got.
It stopped at the step shown above. Everything before that step is listed in the output.
This screen was restarted, so the command wasn\'t run again. Check the status on the main screen.
Dry run passed. Nothing on the phone was changed.

Installed.

The stock policy is backed up as .bak files in /system/etc/selinux. Undo restores from them.

Restart the phone to turn the fix on.
The install checks out: the stock policy backup (.bak) verifies, and /system holds what was installed.\n\nIf you haven\'t restarted since installing, restart to turn the fix on.
Removed. Restart the phone to finish.
Off. The keypad works unfiltered now, and the fix stays off after restarts until you turn it back on.
Running. It stops when the phone restarts, unless Start at boot is on.
Restart now to turn the fix on.
Restart to finish removing the fix.
Type in the box. Every key press and release is listed below, newest first, with its timing, and overlaps, fast repeats and double presses are flagged. Press Back to exit.

Shows how many overlaps and bounces the filter corrected. It needs permission to read the phone's log: press Grant with root, or from a computer:

adb shell pm grant %1$s android.permission.READ_LOGS
adb shell am force-stop %1$s

Then open the app again.
Counts cover what\'s still in the phone\'s log, usually since the last restart.
At its last start the off switch was on, so it exited.
No keydebounce lines in the log yet. Startup messages can get pushed out of the log during boot.
